newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike continues, deal collapses.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike continues, deal collapses.

text.p: Colombian dock workers rejected a preliminary accord Thursday afternoon and voted to continue their two-day-old strike at the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, port authorities said.
The strike has caused chaos with Colombian coffee exports -- more than 60 percent of which are shipped through the port -- and its sugar exports.

Hopes rose that the strike would be lifted in the course of the day on Thursday after cargo operators and dockers' representatives reached an agreement in principle on higher wages and sickness and injury benefits.
But dock workers rejected the wage hike when the deal was put to them at a general assembly late Thursday, a spokesman for private customs agent Pan Servicios said.
All operations are paralysed and no trucks are being allowed to pass picket lines in or out of the port, the spokesman said.

A port authority official said the port was losing $500,000 a day for every day of the strike. John Naranjo, commercial manager of the national Coffee Growers' Federation, said at least 90,000 60-kg bags of coffee destined for export had been caught up in Buenaventura by the action.

"There is no end in sight to this strike. We all thought everything was going to get back to normal this morning. And although we're hoping there's a quick solution, there's no way of knowing," said the Pan Servicios spokesman.
